title: gpu-subpool-claim-atomic-migration-adapter: add tf module, IAM templates, and safe migration helper
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds a tenant-scoped GPU subpool claim Terraform module, a state-adapter helper for atomic TF state migrations, IAM role templates for claim-only principals, and optional helm values to enable the claim controller. No breaking API changes. Recommend follow-up: run upgrade guide and e2e to validate tenant leases.
description: Context: Private installer customers request safer, auditable migrations when reassigning or splitting GPU node subpools between tenants and clusters. Current terraform flows require manual state surgery and risk transient double-claims or dangling leases. This PR introduces a new Terraform module (modules/gpu_subpool_claim) and a small state-adapter tool that emits an atomic migration plan which the installer applies via a single state transaction. The module models a tenant-scoped claim resource, generates consistent immutable lease IDs, and wires up minimal IAM role templates for claim-only principals. The change also adds an optional helm chart flag to enable a lightweight claim-controller in private deployments, plus an integration test that exercises claim lifecycle and rollback semantics. Checklist: 1) Implement tf module with idempotent resources and migration hooks 2) Add state-adapter CLI (Go) that produces a guarded migration plan and validates current state checksum 3) Provide IAM role templates and KMS policy snippets for encrypted lease metadata 4) Add helm values and sample manifest for operator enablement 5) Add integration e2e test and docs/upgrade steps 6) Run terraform fmt and tflint 7) Obtain reviewer approvals. Motivation: reduce human error during tenant rebindings, enable safe roll-forward/roll-back of GPU subpool ownership, and provide an audit trail for infra changes. How it works: the state-adapter reads source and target tfstate snapshots, computes an atomic delta (lease create, lease transfer, subnet binding), and emits a small tfstate import plan that the installer applies with a single state replacement step; the tf module exposes a claim_id and lease_token for runtime reconcilers. Backwards compatibility: modules can be applied side-by-side with existing nodepool modules; the claim-controller is opt-in. Security considerations: lease metadata is encrypted via customer KMS if provided; IAM templates restrict actions to claim-only scopes. Testing summary: local unit tests for module validation, integration e2e across a 3-node ephemeral cluster, and CI terraform plan validation. Migration notes: operators should run the provided state-adapter dry-run, review the produced migration plan, then apply in maintenance window. Related: connects ENG-10294 and SUP-1987.

chore(ci): add terraform plan validation job for gpu claim module

review_comments: Liam Carter: Can you clarify how the adapter ensures no two controllers can claim the same subpool during the transition? Please add an attacker model.

Author (Asha): The adapter requires a pre-check checksum and emits a single replacement state blob; I added a section in docs that explains leader-only application and optimistic concurrency via checksum.
Priya Shah: IAM templates look permissive for the KMS actions; please narrow to Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey rather than full KMS*.
Author (Asha): Updated templates to the minimal set and added integration verify step to ensure encrypted metadata round trips.
Ethan Kim: CI terraform plan failed on first run due to provider version pin mismatch; I see you pinned provider in modules now, thanks. Approving after green CI.
ci_checks: ci/plan: initially failed then rerun and pass
notes_for_ops: Run tools/state-adapter --dry-run against current and target tfstates and review the generated plan. Execute plan during maintenance window. If KMS is enabled, ensure key policy yields Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey to the installer role. Rollback: state-adapter emits inverse operations that can be applied if rollback flag is used.
test_summary: Unit TF validate and tflint run in CI. Integration e2e created ephemeral cluster, deployed claim controller, exercised claim create/transfer/rollback path. Observed no double-claims in 50 trial runs. Test flakes observed under very low timing windows were mitigated by adding pre-check checksum and leader election in controller helm chart.
upgrade_steps: 1) Read docs/upgrade/atomic-gpu-migration.md 2) Run state-adapter with --dry-run to validate plan 3) Enable helm value privateInstaller.enableGpuClaimController if operator wants automated reclaim behavior 4) Apply generated migration plan using installer in maintenance window 5) Verify tenant metrics and lease id consistency in Console
notes: This PR is deliberately conservative: modules are opt-in and default helm values keep existing behavior. The state-adapter is a small trusted helper included in the private-installer bundle and runs with scoped credentials only.
authors_contributor_notes: Reviewed by platform security and infra owners. Follow-up work: add cross-region subpool transfer support and expose a SaaS-side dry-run API for managed hosted migrations.
